summary: Transient multiple auth handshakes after edge failover causing burst latency for tenant
description: Issue summary: BrightDocs reported short-lived end-to-end latency spikes (p95 bursts) immediately after an edge failover event. Impact: customer is seeing increased tail latency for inference requests that are pinned to their dedicated pool; spikes last ~30-90s and correlate with auth token refresh activity. Environment: prod in us-east routing to dedicated pool for BrightDocs (tenant-id: bd-118). Observed: after an edge instance failure and automatic client reroute, we see many concurrent upstream auth exchanges and TLS handshakes, resulting in additional round trips and p95 latency jumps. Expected: failover should preserve residency path and reuse existing auth connections where possible, minimizing extra handshake overhead.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer environment: tenant uses region pinning to us-east with explicit residency; sustained traffic to dedicated pool.
2) Simulate an edge instance termination in us-east (controlled failover or maintenance).
3) Observe upstream routing: control-plane selects a new edge and proxies requests to the dedicated pool.
4) Monitor auth/token refresh rate, TLS handshake counts, and p95/p99 latency metrics during the failover window.
5) Note: failure reproduces intermittently depending on active connections and client keepalive behaviour.
logs: 2026-03-10T14:02:12Z edge-proxy[edge-23] INFO upstream selected: edge-47 (formerly edge-23)
2026-03-10T14:02:13Z auth-service WARN token-refresh concurrent=47 tenant=bd-118 err_rate=0.02 lat_ms=240
Observed metrics: pre-failover p95=180ms, during failover p95=650ms, auth refresh spike +45%
investigation_notes: Edge failover window detected at 2026-03-10T14:02Z; control-plane re-routed connections to a different edge in the same region.
Auth service shows a surge of token refresh operations for tenant bd-118 coincident with edge selection change; many upstream connections did not reuse existing TLS sessions.
Keepalive timeout observed at client side ~20s; control-plane triggered cold re-establish which increased handshake count.
Hypothesis 1: control-plane triggers auth refresh for pinned tenants on edge handoff which causes duplicated refreshes when client also requests a new token.
Hypothesis 2: proxy connection pooling/routing did not properly map persistent session metadata to the new edge causing conn_reuse=false and TLS cost.
Temporary mitigation applied: extended residency-pin TTL and increased keepalive for BrightDocs dedicated pool to reduce number of cold handoffs during maintenance windows.

resolution: Mitigation in progress: temporary keepalive and pin-TTL adjustments applied for BrightDocs which reduced frequency. Engineering to land control-plane patch to suppress duplicate auth refresh on handoff and to ensure session affinity metadata is transferred during edge swap. Post-deploy we'll schedule a controlled failover test with BrightDocs. No permanent fix deployed yet.
